question.text: A straight rigid rod of length l is placed such that its upper point B slides along a smooth vertical wall while its lower point A slides along a horizontal floor. If point A is drawn away from the wall to the left at a constant speed v, determine the downward speed of point B at the precise moment when the rod is inclined at an angle θ to the floor.
conditions: rod maintains contact with both the vertical wall and horizontal floor
lower end A moves horizontally away from the wall at constant velocity v
angle between the rod and the floor is θ

figure.description: A vertical wall and a horizontal floor form a right-angled corner. A straight rod of length l connects the two surfaces, with its upper end B touching the vertical wall and its lower end A resting on the horizontal floor. Point A is moving horizontally to the left with a constant velocity vector labelled v. The angle between the rod and the ground at point A is denoted as θ.

solution.approach: Write the constant-length constraint between the horizontal position of A and the vertical position of B, then differentiate with respect to time.

steps.text: Let x be the horizontal distance of A from the corner and y be the height of B on the wall. The rod length is fixed.
steps.equation: x² + y² = l², with x = l cos θ, y = l sin θ

steps.text: Differentiate the constraint with respect to time.
End A moves away from the wall at the given constant speed v, so dx/dt = v. Substitute x = l cos θ and y = l sin θ.

steps.equation: dy/dt = −v cos θ / sin θ = −v cot θ
steps.why_this_step: The negative sign shows y is decreasing, meaning B moves downward at this rate.

final_answer.value: The velocity of end B is v cot θ, directed downward.

common_mistakes.text: Differentiating x = l cos θ and y = l sin θ but mismatching which trigonometric ratio goes with dx/dt gives v tan θ instead of the correct v cot θ.
